title: Incremental tool shape stability — PRD exploration
body:
Summary

This is an exploratory PRD for a small, high-leverage change to how we stream tool calls and structured outputs over the Hosted API. The idea: introduce an explicit lightweight ‘shape-stability’ layer that surfaces a best-effort structural summary early in a stream and stabilizes as more tokens arrive. This improves SDK ergonomics (typed bindings, quick validation, UI previews) while preserving low-latency incremental streaming.

Why this now

- Customers keep asking for: predictable structured outputs when using streaming + tool integrations (particularly for forms, actions, and multi-step toolflows).
- Current tradeoff: either emit fully-structured JSON at end (high latency / no partial UI preview) or stream plain text fragments (low latency / fragile parsing).
- Many SDKs try to guess shapes client-side and end up with brittle heuristics and occasional UX regressions.

Goal (what success looks like)

- Provide a streaming contract that gives client SDKs an early, machine-readable shape summary and incremental concrete frames that converge to final shape.
- Reduce common integration errors (missing fields, wrong types) by >40% in early adopter integrations (tracked via telemetry).
- Keep median first-byte-to-shape latency <= existing streaming median (no added roundtrips).
- Allow SDKs to render safe previews and apply optimistic tool calls with rollbacks when structure changes.

Non-goals

- Not a redesign of the entire streaming wire protocol. We aim for a minimal backward-compatible extension.
- Not adding heavy validation rules or server-side schema enforcement for all models at launch.

Customer scenarios

- CRM action composer: show a button pane derived from predicted action shape before full completion so users can confirm while the model continues writing details.
- Mobile assistant: show a compact card preview (title+summary) while continuing to stream richer nested content.
- Toolchain adapter: call a downstream API opportunistically with early stabilized fields and patch if additional fields appear.

Design principles

- Minimalism: keep the new framing small and optional so existing clients are unaffected.
- Progressive enhancement: clients that understand the shape layer get better UX; older clients ignore it safely.
- Observability: surface stability metrics (shape_delta_rate, shape_flip_count) for product telemetry and rollouts.

Proposed wire contract (summary)

- New optional field in streaming frames: "shape_frame" (compact, JSON-LD-like summary) emitted as one of the earliest frames.
- shape_frame contains: shape_id (opaque), estimated_fields (list of field names + rough types), tentative (boolean), confidence (0..1), parents (if nested), and minimal hashes for change detection.
- Subsequent frames can be: shape_update (incremental additions), value_diff (delta for field values), final_shape (converged structure) emitted with final=true.
- Legacy: if server does not emit shape_frame, clients fallback to existing incremental text parsing.

Example (conceptual)

- Frame 1: shape_frame {shape_id: abc123, estimated_fields: [ {name:action, type:string}, {name:params,type:object} ], tentative:true, confidence:0.62 }
- Frame 2..N: value_diff for action.title, params.items[0] etc.
- Final frame: final_shape {shape_id: abc123, tentative:false, confidence:0.98}

Key SDK ergonomics patterns enabled

1) Lazy typed binding
- SDK exposes a minimal TypeDescriptor derived from shape_frame. Client can bind UI components to descriptors to show placeholder controls (e.g., text input, select, date) while values are streaming.

2) Optimistic tool invocation with soft rollback
- If shape_frame includes a target endpoint hint and required fields, the SDK can issue an early tool call with current best-effort values and subscribe to patch updates. The server will emit patch/patch-rollback markers if a field changes in incompatible ways.

3) Preview-first rendering
- Mobile/web UIs can render a compact preview using top-level fields from the initial shape_frame and update progressively. This reduces perceived latency.

Operational considerations

- Backward compatibility: shape_frame is optional and must be ignored by older SDKs. On the server, default behavior for models that don’t support shape extraction is to omit shape_frame.
- Bandwidth: shape frames are small (~100–500 bytes typical). We will monitor percent increase in payload size.
- Safety: shape inference must not leak PII. If shape inferencing uses model internals or prompt metadata, apply redaction heuristics.

Telemetry & metrics

Instrument the following:
- shape_emit_rate: percent of streaming calls that include shape_frame.
- shape_converge_time: time from first shape_frame to final_shape.
- shape_flip_count: number of incompatible structural changes after initial commit.
- optimistic_tool_success_rate: percent of early tool calls that did not require rollback.
- sdk_preview_engagement: proxies for product engagement improvements (A/B test).

Rollout plan (phases)

1) Internal experiment (1 month)
- Implement shape_frame in staging for a small set of curated models (low temp, deterministic prompts). Add server-side debug logging.
- Ship SDK alpha bindings (JS + Python) behind feature flag.

2) Beta with partners (2 months)
- Invite 3 customers (solutions & SE-led) to test optimistic tool calls and preview-first rendering. Collect telemetry and developer feedback.

3) Public opt-in (4–6 months)
- Enable feature flag for orgs via console toggle. Provide migration guide, examples, and SDK helpers.

4) Default-on (longer term)
- If metrics and safety checks are green, flip default and iterate on shape richness.

Open implementation details and risks

- How to derive shapes reliably? Options: lightweight model head that emits a shape token; prompt-engineered shim that asks model to emit a compact shape; runtime post-process that parses early tokens. Tradeoffs: accuracy vs engineering complexity. (JIRA: API-742)
- Handling nested/recursive shapes: propose limiting initial launch to 1–2 nesting levels to keep SDKs simple.
- Wire format: prefer simple JSON objects inside our streaming protocol (no new binary format) for interoperability.
- Security: shape inference should not be treated as authoritative for enforcement. Always treat final_shape as eventual source-of-truth.

Developer experience and docs

- Quickstart: "show a preview card in 5 minutes" sample app for web and mobile.
- SDK helpers: TypeDescriptor class, optimisticCall helper, patch handler, preview renderer.
- Debugging: new console view in Redwood Console showing shape events per request and shape_flip_histogram.

Acceptance criteria for GA

- Server emits shape_frame for >=70% of requests for curated models in beta.
- shape_flip_count median <= 1 for production-like prompts.
- No PII leakage incidents in beta (manual and automated checks).
- Developer feedback: >80% of partner SDK evaluators say the preview and optimistic flows reduce integration complexity.

Open questions / TODOs

- Decide initial surface: which models and model sizes to support for shape extraction. (Owners: Miguel + Research)
- Confirm SDK binding API names and cancellation semantics. (Owners: Ethan + DevEx)
- Define storage lifecycle of shape events in telemetry (retention, sampling). (Owner: Product Analytics)

Next steps (next 2 weeks)

- Spike: build two prototypes for shape extraction (prompt shim vs lightweight head) and compare accuracy and latency. (Ethan, Miguel)
- Draft SDK alpha API and internal demo app (Sofia + Ava).
- Create beta partner list and outreach plan (Solutions Eng).

Notes to reviewers

- This is intentionally exploratory — looking for feedback on pragmatic tradeoffs: initial API minimalism vs richer shape fidelity.
- If we proceed, recommend a cross-functional kick-off with Research, Serving Runtime, DevEx, and Solutions Eng.

References and related work

- Related design notes: confluence:prod-hosted-streaming/shape-stability
- Previous attempts: GH: /hosted-api/stream-prefetch-safety (see PR #1041)

Quick sketch of SDK code (JS pseudocode)

- const stream = client.streamCreate({prompt})
- stream.on('shape', desc => renderPreview(desc))
- stream.on('update', diff => applyPatch(diff))
- stream.on('final', full => commitAndDispatchToolCall(full))

-- end of draft --
